questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text:
Modern Workplace, June 5, 2016

The problem of long working hours is a real headache in our country. It kills many people every year (see Figure 1), and many companies are trying to change that. They have at least one "No Overtime Day" in a week, and it is often Wednesday. On "No Overtime Day," workers are asked to leave their offices before 8 p.m. At 8 p.m., companies play the song "There's Always Tomorrow" and turn off all the lights.

However, after the workers walk out of their offices, they don't go home. Some go back later, turn on their table lamps, and keep working, and others find somewhere else to work until very late at night. Restaurants and coffee shops are busier on Wednesday evenings, and they have started selling drinks and meals for these workers.

But why do these people keep working? A study shows that workers who work more hours often have a bigger chance to get paid more and rise higher in their companies. This is true for both men and women (see Figure 2). Working long hours has become a way to show that people are hard-working. Clearly, this must be changed before the problem gets any worse.

There are four important points in the report:
a. What "No Overtime Day" is
b. Why "No Overtime Day" fails
c. Why there is "No Overtime Day" in the country
d. How workers deal with "No Overtime Day"
How are they ordered in the report?
questions.explanation: 第一段先說長工時每年害死很多人，公司想改變（c 為何有「不加班日」），接著介紹「不加班日」的做法（a）；第二段說員工離開辦公室後又回去或換地方繼續工作（d 員工如何應對）；第三段分析大家為何還要繼續工作（b 為何失敗）。順序是 c→a→d→b，選 D。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text:
Modern Workplace, June 5, 2016

The problem of long working hours is a real headache in our country. It kills many people every year (see Figure 1), and many companies are trying to change that. They have at least one "No Overtime Day" in a week, and it is often Wednesday. On "No Overtime Day," workers are asked to leave their offices before 8 p.m. At 8 p.m., companies play the song "There's Always Tomorrow" and turn off all the lights.

However, after the workers walk out of their offices, they don't go home. Some go back later, turn on their table lamps, and keep working, and others find somewhere else to work until very late at night. Restaurants and coffee shops are busier on Wednesday evenings, and they have started selling drinks and meals for these workers.

But why do these people keep working? A study shows that workers who work more hours often have a bigger chance to get paid more and rise higher in their companies. This is true for both men and women (see Figure 2). Working long hours has become a way to show that people are hard-working. Clearly, this must be changed before the problem gets any worse.

What does "this" mean in the report?

options.A: The way workers show they are hard-working.
options.B: Restaurants and coffee shops open until very late at night.
options.C: Workers do not go home when they walk out of the office.
options.D: The number of workers who get paid more and rise higher in the company.

questions.concept_tag: 上下文詞義與指代推測
questions.explanation: this 指的是前一句：Working long hours has become a way to show that people are hard-working（長時間工作變成展現自己很努力的方式），作者認為這種觀念必須改變，選 A。D 是研究結果中的「加薪升遷機會」，不是作者要改變的對象。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text:
Modern Workplace, June 5, 2016

The problem of long working hours is a real headache in our country. It kills many people every year (see Figure 1), and many companies are trying to change that.

Figure 1 (bar chart, "Number of people who die because of long working hours" by year): 2011: 187; 2012: 216; 2013: 196; 2014: 220; 2015: 189.

Figure 2 (line chart, "Percentage (%) of chance to get paid more and rise higher" vs. "Average working hours in a year," x-axis from 1800 to about 2300+ hours): The Women line starts around 4-5% at 1800 hours, rises to about 10% at 1900, about 12% at 2000, peaks around 16% at 2100, dips to about 13% at 2200, then rises sharply to about 22% at 2300 and stays around 22%. The Men line (dashed) starts around 4% at 1800 hours and rises steadily and more gradually, reaching about 14% at 2200 hours and about 13% at 2300+ hours — at around 2200 hours the Men line and Women line are close to each other (about 13-14%).

What can we learn from Figure 1 and Figure 2?

options.A: Long working hours killed more women than men in 2014.
options.B: Long working hours kills more and more workers every year.
options.C: Men usually have a bigger chance to get paid more and rise higher when they work the same hours as women.
options.D: Men and women have almost the same chance to get paid more and rise higher when they work 2,200 hours.

questions.explanation: 從圖 2 可見，工時 2,200 小時時，男女兩條線幾乎重疊（約 13～14%），機會差不多，選 D。A 錯，圖 1 沒有分男女；B 錯，死亡人數有升有降（例如 2014 年 220 人、2015 年降為 189 人）；C 錯，多數工時下女性的線反而比男性高。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text:
Language and Power: Cameroon's Story, By Elisa Grant, 2 Oct 2017

In the modern world, being able to speak English is often a way to get power. However, this is not true for English speakers in Cameroon. To know why things are different in this African country, we need to go back one hundred years.

In 1919, Kamerun (the name of Cameroon at the time) was cut into two parts: one belonged to France, and the other belonged to the UK. In 1960, the French Cameroon became the Republic of Cameroun, and the UK's part joined it in 1961. The new country changed its name to the Federal Republic of Cameroon. Although both French and English are Cameroon's official languages, only around 20% of its people speak English. Also, the government has been in French speakers' hands since the two parts became one country.

Which map is most likely the map of Cameroon in 1962?
(A) A map showing the whole country as a single region labeled "Kamerun."
(B) A map showing the country split into two regions: a smaller western region labeled "UK's Cameroon" and a larger eastern region labeled "French Cameroon."
(C) A map showing the country split into two regions: a smaller western region labeled "UK's Cameroon" and a larger eastern region labeled "Republic of Cameroun."
(D) A map showing the whole country as a single region labeled "Federal Republic of Cameroon."

options.A: A map with the whole country as one region labeled "Kamerun."
options.B: A map with two regions: "UK's Cameroon" (smaller, west) and "French Cameroon" (larger, east).
options.C: A map with two regions: "UK's Cameroon" (smaller, west) and "Republic of Cameroun" (larger, east).
options.D: A map with the whole country as one region labeled "Federal Republic of Cameroon."

questions.explanation: 文章說英國管轄的部分在 1961 年併入 Republic of Cameroun，新國家隨即改名為 Federal Republic of Cameroon；到了 1962 年已是統一的一個國家，選 D。A 是 1919 年以前的 Kamerun，B 是 1919～1960 年英法分治，C 是 1960～1961 年兩部分尚未合併的情形。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text:
Language and Power: Cameroon's Story, By Elisa Grant, 2 Oct 2017

For a long time, Cameroon's English speakers have felt they are not welcome in their own country. For example, it is very difficult for them to find jobs in the government, and they are often asked to speak French in business and at official events. They have become more resentful at the government and decided to fight for themselves. Since last year, the English speakers have tried to build their own country. Yesterday, they said in a public meeting that they were not part of Cameroon anymore. They are now a new country, "Ambazonia." When the police tried to stop the meeting, at least eight people were killed.

What does resentful mean in the reading?
questions.concept_tag: 上下文詞義與指代推測
questions.explanation: 英語使用者在政府難找工作、常被要求說法語，覺得在自己國家不受歡迎，後文又說他們決定為自己抗爭、甚至宣布建立新國家，可見 resentful 是「憤恨不平、生氣的」，選 B。sad、worried 雖是負面情緒，但接不上後面「起來抗爭」的行動。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text:
Language and Power: Cameroon's Story, By Elisa Grant, 2 Oct 2017

For a long time, Cameroon's English speakers have felt they are not welcome in their own country. For example, it is very difficult for them to find jobs in the government, and they are often asked to speak French in business and at official events. They have become more resentful at the government and decided to fight for themselves. Since last year, the English speakers have tried to build their own country. Yesterday, they said in a public meeting that they were not part of Cameroon anymore. They are now a new country, "Ambazonia." When the police tried to stop the meeting, at least eight people were killed.

What does Cameroon's government most likely think of Ambazonia?

options.A: It plans to do business with Ambazonia.
options.B: It needs Ambazonia for money and help.
options.C: It does not want to be part of Ambazonia.
options.D: It does not agree that Ambazonia is a country.

questions.explanation: 英語使用者宣布成立新國家 Ambazonia 時，警察出面阻止集會，甚至造成至少八人死亡，可見喀麥隆政府不承認 Ambazonia 是一個國家，選 D。C 說反了，是 Ambazonia 不想再屬於喀麥隆；文中也沒有提到與它做生意或需要它幫助。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text:
Language and Power: Cameroon's Story, By Elisa Grant, 2 Oct 2017

In the modern world, being able to speak English is often a way to get power. However, this is not true for English speakers in Cameroon. To know why things are different in this African country, we need to go back one hundred years.

In 1919, Kamerun (the name of Cameroon at the time) was cut into two parts: one belonged to France, and the other belonged to the UK. In 1960, the French Cameroon became the Republic of Cameroun, and the UK's part joined it in 1961. The new country changed its name to the Federal Republic of Cameroon. Although both French and English are Cameroon's official languages, only around 20% of its people speak English. Also, the government has been in French speakers' hands since the two parts became one country.

What does Elisa Grant try to tell readers by talking about the history of Cameroon?

options.A: Why speaking English is a way to get power.
options.B: Why English speakers in Cameroon have less power.
options.C: Why the two parts of Cameroon became one country.
options.D: Why only 20% of the people in Cameroon speak English.

questions.explanation: 作者開頭說：在現代世界會說英語常能取得權力，但在喀麥隆不是這樣，要了解原因得回顧百年歷史；接著說明英語人口只佔約 20%，政府一直掌握在說法語的人手中。所以談歷史是為了解釋喀麥隆說英語的人為何權力較小，選 B。D 的 20% 只是歷史敘述中的一個細節，不是作者的目的。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text:
THE SOUTHEND TRAIL has been popular with nature lovers for years. The 120-km trail passes beautiful lakes, crosses rivers, and goes through mountains and hills. This gives bird lovers some of the best places for birdwatching. The trail also takes you to the Southend Museum and to two famous castles, Edward Castle and Sloan Castle.

It's best to plan one day for one part of the trail and start your hike early in the morning, because each part takes at least seven hours. If you don't want to walk, you can bike, but make sure you stay on the main trail, because the side trails are not wide enough for biking.

There are two types of lodging for visitors. Camping is popular in summer, but it is only allowed on a few campgrounds (see the map). A more comfortable one is to stay at a hotel in one of the towns. You can find some very nice ones that also have breakfast.

(Map of Southend Trail: four towns — Cove (top), Dova (right), Berk (left), Kint (bottom) — connected by a loop-shaped main trail divided into Part 1 (Cove-Dova), Part 2 (Dova-Kint), Part 3 (Kint-Berk), and Part 4 (Berk-Cove). Two dashed side trails branch off the main trail: Part 4a near Berk leading to Edward Castle, and Part 2a near Kint leading to Sloan Castle. The Southend Museum is near Kint. Mountains are clustered in the middle of the loop, a river winds through the middle-to-lower area near Berk/Dova/Kint, and campgrounds (fire icons) are marked near Edward Castle/Part 1 area and near Part 2.)

What is recommended to people who are visiting the Southend Trail?

options.C: Hiking one part of the trail a day.
options.D: Visiting the museum in the morning.

questions.explanation: 文中建議 It's best to plan one day for one part of the trail，因為每一段至少要走七小時，所以推薦一天走一段，選 C。A 錯，露營只能在指定營地；B 錯，側步道太窄不能騎車；D 錯，文中說的是「早上出發健行」，不是早上去博物館。
questions.text_issue: question_text 的地圖描述寫 Part 2a 通往 Sloan Castle，但原圖中 Sloan Castle 位於主步道 Part 2 外側，Part 2a 是環內的側步道（不影響本題答案）。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text:
THE SOUTHEND TRAIL has been popular with nature lovers for years. The 120-km trail passes beautiful lakes, crosses rivers, and goes through mountains and hills.

There are two types of lodging for visitors. Camping is popular in summer, but it is only allowed on a few campgrounds (see the map). A more comfortable one is to stay at a hotel in one of the towns. You can find some very nice ones that also have breakfast.

What does lodging mean in the reading?
questions.concept_tag: 上下文詞義與指代推測
questions.explanation: 文中說 lodging 有兩種：露營，以及更舒適的「住在鎮上的旅館」，兩者都是過夜的地方，所以 lodging 指「住宿的地方」，選 B。提到旅館附早餐只是補充，lodging 本身不是一餐。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text:
THE SOUTHEND TRAIL has been popular with nature lovers for years. The 120-km trail passes beautiful lakes, crosses rivers, and goes through mountains and hills. This gives bird lovers some of the best places for birdwatching. The trail also takes you to the Southend Museum and to two famous castles, Edward Castle and Sloan Castle.

(Map of Southend Trail: four towns — Cove (top), Dova (right), Berk (left), Kint (bottom) — connected by a loop-shaped main trail divided into Part 1 (Cove-Dova), Part 2 (Dova-Kint), Part 3 (Kint-Berk), and Part 4 (Berk-Cove). Two dashed side trails branch off the main trail: Part 4a near Berk leading to Edward Castle (near the Part 4/Part 4a area, upper-left of the map), and Part 2a near Kint leading to Sloan Castle (near the Part 2/Part 2a area, lower-right of the map). The Southend Museum is near Kint. Mountains are clustered in the middle of the loop, and a river winds through the map from near the Part 1/Part 4 area (upper-middle, near Cove/Berk) down through the middle toward Dova and Kint.)

Kaylen will start his trip from Cove. He plans to visit one of the old castles. He also wants to go birdwatching near the river. Which parts of the trail should Kaylen go on?
questions.explanation: 看地圖：從 Cove 出發走 Part 1（Cove－Dova），在快到 Dova 時會跨過河流，可以在河邊賞鳥；接著走 Part 2（Dova－Kint），主步道旁就是 Sloan Castle，所以選 A。Part 4、4a 雖經過 Edward Castle 但沒有經過河流；Part 2a 是環內側步道，不經過城堡；C 的 Part 2、3 也不是從 Cove 出發。
questions.text_issue: question_text 的地圖描述有誤：寫 Part 2a 通往 Sloan Castle（原圖城堡在主步道 Part 2 旁），並寫河流從 Cove/Berk 附近的 Part 1/Part 4 區流向 Dova、Kint（原圖河流是從 Dova 北邊斜穿中央到 Berk 南邊，跨過 Part 1 與 Part 3，不經過 Part 4），會誤導本題判斷。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text:
English words are made of 26 letters, and palindromes and anagrams are two kinds of word games about spelling. A palindrome is a word or a sentence that reads the same from left to right or from right to left, __40__, "eye," "Bob," "my gym," and "Was it a car or a cat I saw?" An anagram of a word or words is made by putting the letters of the word or words in a different way. Look at the words and their anagrams below. Can you think of other possible anagrams of these words?

Examples shown: earth → (letters e,a,r,h,t) → heart; between → (letters b,e,e,e,n,t,w) → been wet; a tie → (letters a,i,t,e) → I eat; mistake → (letters m,t,i,a,e,s,k) → __41__.

Anagrams are often longer words that don't really mean anything but are fun to say. Sometimes they can even mean something __42__, like when a common word, "restaurant," becomes "Eat rats, run!"

Actually, palindromes and anagrams are __43__. Palindromes can be used to learn mathematics and make music. Anagrams are also a good way to hide something. In history, people often hid their important studies in anagrams. Can you think of any other way to use them?

40.
questions.explanation: 空格前定義什麼是 palindrome（迴文），空格後列出 eye、Bob、my gym 等實際例子，所以用 for example（例如）。in fact 是「事實上」、at first 是「起初」、of course 是「當然」，都不能用來引出例子。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text:
English words are made of 26 letters, and palindromes and anagrams are two kinds of word games about spelling. A palindrome is a word or a sentence that reads the same from left to right or from right to left, __40__, "eye," "Bob," "my gym," and "Was it a car or a cat I saw?" An anagram of a word or words is made by putting the letters of the word or words in a different way. Look at the words and their anagrams below.

Examples shown: earth → (letters e,a,r,h,t) → heart; between → (letters b,e,e,e,n,t,w) → been wet; a tie → (letters a,i,t,e) → I eat; mistake → (letters m,t,i,a,e,s,k) → __41__.

41.
questions.explanation: anagram 必須用完全相同的字母重新排列。mistake 的字母是 m、i、s、t、a、k、e，it makes 正好是這七個字母各用一次，選 C。take sit 多了一個 t；Ms Easy 有 y；me steak 有兩個 e 且沒有 i。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text:
English words are made of 26 letters, and palindromes and anagrams are two kinds of word games about spelling. Look at the words and their anagrams (earth→heart, between→been wet, a tie→I eat, mistake→ (an anagram)).

Anagrams are often longer words that don't really mean anything but are fun to say. Sometimes they can even mean something __42__, like when a common word, "restaurant," becomes "Eat rats, run!"

42.
questions.explanation: restaurant 重組成 Eat rats, run!（吃老鼠，快跑！），意思很古怪好笑，所以說 anagram 有時甚至會變成「奇怪的」意思，選 A strange。這句話和好吃（delicious）、重要（important）都沾不上邊。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text:
English words are made of 26 letters, and palindromes and anagrams are two kinds of word games about spelling.

Anagrams are often longer words that don't really mean anything but are fun to say. Sometimes they can even mean something important, like when a common word, "restaurant," becomes "Eat rats, run!"

Actually, palindromes and anagrams are __43__. Palindromes can be used to learn mathematics and make music. Anagrams are also a good way to hide something. In history, people often hid their important studies in anagrams. Can you think of any other way to use them?

43.

options.D: not first used to learn words

questions.explanation: 空格後說迴文可以用來學數學、創作音樂，重組字可以用來隱藏東西，歷史上還有人把重要研究藏在其中，都在說明它們有遊戲以外的用途，所以選 A more than just games（不只是遊戲）。後文沒有提到公開玩、流行程度下降或最初用途。
questions.text_issue: question_text 把第 42 題空格直接填成 important（寫成 mean something important），但第 42 題正確答案是 strange，等於在文章中放進錯誤答案。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Look at the picture. The man is holding a ______ of grapes in his hands. [Picture: a man in an apron holding a basket full of grapes, with a box of grapes on the ground beside him.]
questions.explanation: 圖中男子雙手捧著的是一個有提把的籃子，裡面裝滿葡萄，a basket of grapes＝一籃葡萄。地上那個才是箱子(box)，別被誤導選 D；bag 袋子、bowl 碗都不符合圖片。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Dennis enjoys ______ in public. He is proud of his beautiful voice.
questions.explanation: 第二句說他以自己美妙的歌聲(beautiful voice)為傲，可推知他喜歡在公開場合唱歌，enjoy 後接動名詞 singing。dancing 跳舞、drawing 畫畫、shopping 購物都和「聲音」無關。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Mrs. Johnson can't hear very well. If you need to talk to her, you must ______ .
questions.explanation: Johnson 太太聽力不好(can't hear very well)，所以跟她說話時必須大聲喊，選 shout。C listen 是「聽的人」做的事，不是說話者該做的；explain 解釋、hurry 趕快都不合語意。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: People got very excited when they watched Ms. Smith ______ at the party.
questions.concept_tag: 分詞構句與感官使役動詞
questions.explanation: 感官動詞 watch 的句型是「watch＋受詞＋原形動詞／V-ing」，V-ing 表示看到動作正在進行，故選 dancing。感官動詞後不能接過去式 danced、has danced，也不能接 to dance。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: I tried on these shoes in several different ______ , and I thought the white pair looked best on me.
questions.explanation: 後半句說「我覺得白色那雙最好看」，white 是顏色，可知試穿的是不同顏色(colors)的鞋。prices 價錢、shapes 形狀、sizes 尺寸都無法和「白色那雙」呼應。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Rex did not feel the earthquake this morning. He ______ in the park at the time.
questions.explanation: 地震發生「那時候」(at the time)他正在公園慢跑，所以沒感覺到，要用過去進行式 was jogging 表示過去某個時間點正在進行的動作。A 過去簡單式無法表達「正在」；C 現在完成式、D would jog 時態都不合。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Mr. Lee has worked in the same store for ten years; he's never thought about ______ his job.
questions.explanation: 在同一家店工作了十年，從沒想過「換」工作，change one's job＝換工作；介系詞 about 後面接動名詞 changing。finding 找工作、starting 開始工作都不合「已經工作十年」的情境。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: I didn't take the bus today because it was ______ . All the seats were taken and a lot of students were standing.
questions.explanation: 後句說座位都被坐滿、很多學生站著，表示公車客滿，所以選 full。dirty 髒、fast 快、wrong 錯的都無法從後句推出。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Don't go away when you're cooking, ______ the food might burn.
questions.explanation: 「煮東西時別走開，否則食物可能會燒焦」，祈使句＋or＝否則。but 但是、if 如果、so 所以都不符合語意（祈使句＋and 則是「就會」，也不對）。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Jerry wanted to know ______ he was kicked off the soccer team, but no one gave him a good reason.
questions.explanation: 後半句說「沒有人給他一個好理由(reason)」，可見他想知道的是被踢出球隊的「原因」，用 why 引導間接問句。where、when 問地點與時間，whether 是「是否」，都無法對應 reason。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Jenny is already forty, doesn't have a job and often makes trouble for her parents. To them, she is really a(n) ______ .
questions.explanation: Jenny 四十歲了還沒工作、又常給父母惹麻煩，對父母來說她真是個「令人頭痛的人」，headache 可比喻讓人煩惱的人或事。daughter 字面上雖成立但無法呼應「惹麻煩」；example 榜樣、gift 禮物則語意相反。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Ed and Jill ______ camping this weekend, so they have to finish their homework by Friday.
questions.explanation: 句中有未來時間 this weekend，且後句說「所以他們得在週五前寫完功課」，表示已經計畫好的未來活動，可用現在進行式 are going (camping) 表未來。went、were going 是過去式，have gone 是現在完成式，都和這週末的安排不合。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Doraemon, a blue Japanese robot cat, has hated mice since his ears ______ by a mouse.
questions.explanation: 耳朵是「被」老鼠咬，要用被動語態 be＋p.p.；since 後面接過去發生的事，用過去式，所以是 were bitten（bite 的過去分詞是 bitten）。D have bitten 是主動語態，意思會變成耳朵去咬別人。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: If we play some interesting games in class, there ______ more fun in learning English.
questions.concept_tag: 數量詞與主詞動詞一致
questions.explanation: 「there＋be 動詞」表示「有」；if 條件子句用現在式，主要子句用未來式，所以是 there will be。there 句型不能接 has 或 will have；A are 缺少未來的意思，而且 fun 是不可數名詞也不能用 are。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: The ______ of this shop was so bad; I never got any answer after I emailed them my questions.
questions.explanation: 寄 email 問問題卻從來沒得到回覆，表示這家店的「服務」很差，service＝服務。item 商品、business 生意、price 價格都和「不回覆問題」無關。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: It's not easy to see those islands clearly from here on sunny days, and it's even less ______ to see them on cloudy days.
questions.explanation: 晴天都不容易看清楚那些島了，陰天就「更不可能」看到，even less possible＝更不可能。若選 A，even less difficult 會變成「更不困難」＝更容易，語意正好相反，是最常見的陷阱。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Do you remember the CD I was looking for for months? I ______ found it in a small shop. Look, here it is!
questions.explanation: 找了好幾個月的 CD，「終於」在一家小店找到了，後面還說「你看，就在這裡！」，所以用 finally。almost 幾乎（表示沒找到）、still 仍然、even 甚至都不合語意。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Business at Jane's shop has not been good these days. And the new supermarket across the street only makes things ______ .
questions.explanation: 店裡生意本來就不好，對街又開了一家新超市搶生意，只會讓情況「更糟」，make things worse＝使情況更糟。easier、more convenient 都是對店家有利的說法，more boring 則不合語意。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Scott wasn't sure if the young woman before him was ______ pulled him out of a car on fire.
questions.explanation: was 後面需要一個名詞當補語，這個名詞再由關係子句「把他從著火的車裡拉出來」修飾，所以是 the one who pulled him out…。A 只有 who，缺少先行詞；B 缺關係代名詞，was 和 pulled 兩個動詞無法連接；C 多了 she 仍然缺連接詞。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: I ______ swimming for several years before I went to this high school. I gave it up because of heavy schoolwork.
questions.explanation: before I went to this high school 是過去的時間，而且後句說已經放棄了(gave it up)，所以練游泳是過去的事，用過去式 practiced。A 現在完成式表示持續到現在，和「已經放棄」矛盾；B 現在進行式、D would practice 也都不合。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Frank Kane is so good in the movie that many people ______ he will win the best actor prize.
questions.explanation: 他在電影裡表現得太好，所以很多人「預期」他會拿到最佳男演員獎，expect＋子句＝預料、期待…。forget 忘記、notice 注意到、plan 計畫都不符合語意。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: The new medicine that just came out on the market ______ thousands of lives.
questions.explanation: 主詞是 The new medicine，that just came out on the market 是修飾它的形容詞子句，整句還缺主要動詞，所以選 has saved（已經拯救了數千條生命）。C saving、D to save 都不是完整的動詞；A and saved 前面沒有可以對等連接的動詞。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Now I often think of those days with Pip, my pet dog. When I read in my room, he ______ quietly beside me.
questions.explanation: Now I often think of those days 表示現在在回想「過去那段日子」，當時 Pip 常常過來安靜坐在身旁，是過去的習慣，用 used to＋原形動詞。B comes and sits 是現在的習慣，但這已經是回憶；A 未來式、C 現在完成式也都不合。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Four Seasons' Kitchen. Opening hours: 2:00~8:00 pm Tuesday~Sunday (We're closed on Mondays and the second Sunday of every month.) Sandwiches: Beach Sandwich $70 (Bread + Fish + Lettuce); Garden Sandwich $80 (Bread + Chicken + Tomatoes + Cheese); Sunday Sandwich $90 (Bread + Egg + Steak + Ham + Lettuce). Drinks: Spring Rain $50 (Green Tea + Guava + Lemon); Summer Rainbow $60 (Milk + Watermelon); Autumn Wind $60 (Black Tea + Apple); Winter Snow $70 (Chocolate Milk + Ice Cream). Good News: Star-Collecting Plan — You get a star by ordering a sandwich or a drink. With 15 stars, you can get a $60 drink for free! Amy went to Four Seasons' Kitchen with her mother after she collected 15 stars. They ordered two Garden Sandwiches, an Autumn Wind, and a Winter Snow. After using the stars, how much did they pay for their meals?
questions.explanation: 兩份 Garden Sandwich $80×2＝$160，加上 Autumn Wind $60、Winter Snow $70，共 $290。15 顆星可以免費換一杯 $60 的飲料，所以 Autumn Wind 不用付錢：290－60＝$230。誤選 A 是忘了扣掉星星；Winter Snow 是 $70，不能用星星換。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Four Seasons' Kitchen. Opening hours: 2:00~8:00 pm Tuesday~Sunday (We're closed on Mondays and the second Sunday of every month.) Amy wants to bring her friends to Four Seasons' Kitchen in August. She looks at her calendar to pick a time to go there. Which are the time and date she can choose? Calendar (August): Aug 2-5 Summer camp; Aug 6-10 Summer camp; Aug 12 Party at Ken's; Aug 13-19 Family trip to the South; Aug 20-26 Family trip to the South; Aug 27 Clean the house; Aug 29 School begins; Aug 30 Baseball game at 6.
questions.explanation: 餐廳營業時間是週二到週日下午 2 點到晚上 8 點，週一和每月第二個週日公休。8/11 是週五，月曆上沒有行程，下午 5 點也在營業時間內，所以選 B。A 晚上 8:30 已經打烊；C 8/13 是八月的第二個週日，公休；D 8/28 是週一，公休。
questions.text_issue: JSON 的月曆轉寫沒有標出星期（8/1 週二、8/13 週日、8/28 週一），無法判斷公休日；且圖上家族旅行是 8/14 起，不是 8/13。

questions.question_text: Class: Science  Date: 2020/6/17. What Should You Do If You Find a Baby Bird Out of the Nest? If the bird is HURT: Call the animal center (0-123-4567). OR Carefully pick the bird up and take it to an animal hospital. (Keep it warm and don't give it any food!) If the bird is NOT HURT: If it has FEW FEATHERS: + You CAN reach the nest → Put the bird back. + If you CAN'T find or reach the nest → Call the animal center. If it has FEATHERS: + Just leave it there! (It's learning how to fly!) Note: People believe birds will give up their babies if they have the smell of people on them. WRONG! Birds don't care! According to the notes, which is the WRONG way to help a baby bird that is out of its nest?

options.A: Feed it before you take it to a hospital.
options.B: Leave it alone if it is not hurt and has feathers.
options.C: Call the animal center if you can't find its nest.
options.D: Put it back in its nest if it is not hurt and has few feathers.

questions.explanation: 筆記寫受傷的鳥送醫時要「保暖、不要餵牠任何食物」(don't give it any food)，所以 A 先餵牠再送醫是錯誤做法。B、C、D 分別對應筆記中「有羽毛就留在原地」、「找不到巢就打給動物中心」、「羽毛少且搆得到巢就放回去」，都是正確做法。

questions.question_text: FROM THE FARM TO THE TABLE: FIVE STAGES OF FOOD WASTE. Stage 1 (On the farm): Throw away food of wrong shapes or sizes; Grow more food than the market needs. Stage 2 (On the road): Do not have refrigerators to keep food fresh; Lose food that falls off the truck. Stage 3 (At factories): Do not have enough machines to make, keep and pack food; Throw away food of wrong shapes or sizes. Stage 4 (At stores): Throw away food that does not look fresh; Order more food than they can sell. Stage 5 (At homes or restaurants): Buy too much food; Throw away food when it is still safe to eat. What percentage of food in each area is wasted at each stage in 2014? North America & Oceania (32.4% total): Stage1 10.5%, Stage2 3.5%, Stage3 3.4%, Stage4 2.4%, Stage5 12.6%. Europe (31.4% total): Stage1 11.3%, Stage2 3.4%, Stage3 3.9%, Stage4 2.2%, Stage5 10.6%. South & Southeast Asia (28.2% total): Stage1 8.7%, Stage2 9.6%, Stage3 2.7%, Stage4 4.6%, Stage5 2.6%. According to the reading, which is one of the reasons for food waste?

options.A: Stores do not know how to pack food well.
options.B: Farmers do not have enough machines to collect food.
options.C: There is no refrigerator on the truck to keep food fresh.
options.D: Factories do not have enough trucks to carry food to stores.

questions.explanation: Stage 2（運送途中）寫著 Do not have refrigerators to keep food fresh，也就是卡車上沒有冰箱保鮮，對應 C。A 包裝的問題屬於工廠(Stage 3)，不是商店；B 農場的問題是丟掉形狀、大小不對的食物和種太多，不是缺機器；D 工廠缺的是機器，不是卡車。

questions.question_text: Sometimes when the rain falls hard and fast on you, it might hurt a little. But what happens when it hits a mosquito? A 2012 study says when a raindrop falls on a mosquito, it's like when a bus hits a person. Besides, the little insect is hit by a raindrop about once every 20 seconds. So why don't we see many dead mosquitoes after it rains? A mosquito is as big as a raindrop, but it is much lighter — 0.002 g only. This saves its life in raindrop attacks. Because the mosquito is so light, when it is hit by a raindrop, it won't experience a force that is strong enough to kill it. The study also found that when a mosquito is hit by a raindrop, the insect is pushed by the raindrop and falls together with it. But the mosquito doesn't get wet easily because it is covered with hairs which keep off water. After dropping about 6 cm, it will roll off the raindrop and fly away. However, this trick isn't always successful. If the mosquito flies too low when it is hit by the raindrop, it won't have time to fly off. Then it will hit the ground and meet its death. What is the trick that the mosquito uses in rain?

options.A: It shakes its body fast enough to get water off.
options.B: It drops with the raindrop and then rolls off it.
options.C: It flies behind the raindrop and pushes it away.
options.D: It rides on the raindrop and lands on the ground.

questions.explanation: 第三段說蚊子被雨滴打中時，會跟著雨滴一起往下掉，大約 6 公分後就從雨滴上滾開(roll off)飛走，這就是牠的 trick，選 B。A 甩掉水、C 推開雨滴文中都沒提；D 若跟著落到地面反而會死。

questions.question_text: You probably have heard Beethoven's famous piano piece "For Elise," but do you know who "Elise" was? One story is that Elise was Elisabeth Röckel. She once sang in Beethoven's opera Fidelio, and the two became very good friends. Beethoven called her "Elise." When Röckel was leaving the city of Vienna, Beethoven wrote "For Elise" to say goodbye to her. Another story is that Elise was Therese Malfatti. Beethoven was in love with her. He wrote a piece for her and put "For Therese" on the manuscript. Malfatti kept the manuscript and left it to her family when she died. Later, a man copied the manuscript and wrote "For Elise" by mistake. There is another possible Elise: Elise Barensfeld. She learned the piano from Malfatti, the same Malfatti in the second story. To help Malfatti, Beethoven wrote the piece for her to use to teach Barensfeld. These are just some guesses about who Elise was. We may never know the right answer. No one knew about the piece until 1867, when the manuscript was found. This was 40 years after Beethoven's death, so he wasn't around to tell us who Elise was. Only one thing is for sure: "For Elise" will always be enjoyed. What do the three stories in the reading all talk about?
questions.explanation: 三個故事分別是：為了和 Röckel 道別而寫、寫給所愛的 Therese 後被抄錯曲名、為了幫 Malfatti 教 Barensfeld 而寫，都在說明貝多芬「為什麼寫」這首曲子（以及 Elise 是誰），選 D。A 只有第二個故事談到愛情；B、C 文中都沒提。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Jesse Cohen Says (Family 365, Jul. 2017): Which would you give a boy for his birthday, a toy truck or a doll? If you choose the truck, well, you're not alone. Most people think that some toys are for boys and some are for girls. We might pick building toys for boys and kitchen toys for girls. But why do we do this? Are boys and girls really born with different interests in toys? No, they are not. Children start to show different interests in toys at age three, but only because at this time, they begin to learn about gender and to follow what others of their gender do. If you give a girl kitchen toys, she will think they are girls' toys because she sees other girls playing with them. But if you give a girl a toy car and show her a group of girls who are playing with cars, she'll play with the toy car and think it is a girls' toy. This "watch and follow" habit often becomes a rule for both boys and girls in choosing the "right" toys. However, this rule can be bad for children. Different toys teach children different things. Dolls help with their early language use, and building toys are good for learning math and science. By playing with different toys, children can find out what they are interested in or what they are good at. If they only play one kind of toy, they may lose this important chance. They may also get a wrong idea about what boys or girls are able to do. Some doctors worry that children may use the same kind of thinking when they look for jobs in the future. If they do, they may miss something more important than just getting a chance to play with different toys. They may miss many, perhaps better, chances in life. What idea does Jesse Cohen talk about in the reading?

options.A: Not all kinds of toys are helpful for children's learning.
options.B: Parents should give their children the right toys for their age.
options.C: Children should learn about their gender from playing with toys.
options.D: We should not let gender decide which toys children can play with.

questions.explanation: 作者指出孩子並非天生對玩具有性別偏好，只是模仿同性別的人，而這種「看了就跟著做」的規則對孩子不好，會讓他們錯失探索興趣與未來機會，所以主旨是不該讓性別決定孩子玩什麼玩具，選 D。C 正好和作者立場相反；A、B 文中沒有這樣主張。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Marie Colvin was a world-famous war reporter. She was born in New York, USA, in 1956 and died in Homs, Syria, in 2012. When she was a student at Yale University, Colvin decided that she wanted to be a reporter in the future. She joined the Sunday Times, a UK newspaper, in 1985 and soon became its Middle East reporter. Besides the Middle East, she also reported from other parts of the world: Chechnya, Kosovo and Sri Lanka, for example. When she was reporting on the war in Sri Lanka, she lost her left eye. But that never stopped her. She still went to dangerous places that few reporters wanted to visit and stayed when others left. Colvin showed great empathy in her stories. For her, war reporting was not just some quick interviews and a few photos. She wrote about real people and their real lives. Her writing made you feel so strongly about these people's stories, just like they were your own. She hoped that through her work the world would understand what really happened in war, and would take action to stop the fighting. On February 22, 2012, the day after she gave her report on the war in Homs, Colvin was killed when the house she was staying in was attacked. She always knew what price a war reporter might have to pay. She already lost an eye before. This time, she gave her life to the work she could not give up — telling the true stories to the world. What is the reading mostly about?
questions.explanation: 全文從她在大學立志當記者、進入 Sunday Times、到各地報導戰爭、在斯里蘭卡失去一隻眼睛，一直寫到在 Homs 殉職，描述的是她的職業生涯，選 B。A 只是其中一部分；C、D 都只是文章裡的一小段，範圍太窄。

options.B: They like to read other people's life stories.

options.D: They are good at helping people change their own lives.

questions.concept_tag: 上下文詞義與指代推測
questions.explanation: 文中說她寫真實的人與生活，讓讀者對那些人的故事感同身受，好像是自己的故事一樣，可推知 empathy 是「能理解別人的感受」（同理心），選 C。A、B、D 只是抓了文中「照片」「人生故事」等字眼，不是這個字的意思。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Marie Colvin was a world-famous war reporter. She was born in New York, USA, in 1956 and died in Homs, Syria, in 2012. When she was a student at Yale University, Colvin decided that she wanted to be a reporter in the future. She joined the Sunday Times, a UK newspaper, in 1985 and soon became its Middle East reporter. Besides the Middle East, she also reported from other parts of the world: Chechnya, Kosovo and Sri Lanka, for example. When she was reporting on the war in Sri Lanka, she lost her left eye. But that never stopped her. She still went to dangerous places that few reporters wanted to visit and stayed when others left. Colvin showed great empathy in her stories. For her, war reporting was not just some quick interviews and a few photos. She wrote about real people and their real lives. Her writing made you feel so strongly about these people's stories, just like they were your own. She hoped that through her work the world would understand what really happened in war, and would take action to stop the fighting. On February 22, 2012, the day after she gave her report on the war in Homs, Colvin was killed when the house she was staying in was attacked. She always knew what price a war reporter might have to pay. She already lost an eye before. This time, she gave her life to the work she could not give up — telling the true stories to the world. Which is true about Marie Colvin?

options.A: The chance to study at Yale made her leave her job in the Middle East.
options.B: The experience in Sri Lanka did not change her way of reporting news.
options.C: She was killed in Homs when she was interviewing soldiers there for her report.
options.D: She was not sure what to do in the future until she worked for the Sunday Times.

questions.explanation: 她在斯里蘭卡失去左眼，但文中說 that never stopped her，她仍然去危險的地方、在別人離開時留下來，表示這段經歷沒有改變她報導新聞的方式，選 B。A 順序顛倒，她是在 Yale 讀書時就決定當記者；C 她是在住的房子遭攻擊時身亡，不是在採訪士兵；D 她在大學時就確定了未來方向。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: NiceReads (https://www.nicereads.com.tw/comments). Speaking American is a great book! Lucia Leisure ★★★★★. I just love Josh Katz's new book! It's about __42__ in different parts of the US. The information in the book was collected from the quiz that Katz built on the website in 2013. The quiz asked what words people use for something, and their answers showed interesting facts. For example, there are different names for sports shoes. In most parts of the US, people say "tennis shoes." In the northeast of the country, people wear "sneakers." In some towns, "tennis shoes" and "sneakers" become "gym shoes." The use of words tells us where people are from, like Katz's book says. But in my experience, it also shows __43__. My family has lived in New York since my grandparents. It's not surprising that I say "sneakers." But my grandfather says "plimsolls," and my daughter says "kicks" or "vans." Maybe Katz can study this difference for his next book. Question 42: choose the best word(s) for blank 42.

options.D: what words are often spelled differently

questions.explanation: 後文舉例說明同樣是運動鞋，各地有 tennis shoes、sneakers、gym shoes 等不同叫法，可知這本書講的是美國各地「東西怎麼稱呼」，選 A。D 講的是同一個字拼法不同，但文中是用不同的字；B、C 與內容無關。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: NiceReads (https://www.nicereads.com.tw/comments). Speaking American is a great book! Lucia Leisure ★★★★★. I just love Josh Katz's new book! It's about __42__ in different parts of the US. The information in the book was collected from the quiz that Katz built on the website in 2013. The quiz asked what words people use for something, and their answers showed interesting facts. For example, there are different names for sports shoes. In most parts of the US, people say "tennis shoes." In the northeast of the country, people wear "sneakers." In some towns, "tennis shoes" and "sneakers" become "gym shoes." The use of words tells us where people are from, like Katz's book says. But in my experience, it also shows __43__. My family has lived in New York since my grandparents. It's not surprising that I say "sneakers." But my grandfather says "plimsolls," and my daughter says "kicks" or "vans." Maybe Katz can study this difference for his next book. Question 43: choose the best word(s) for blank 43.

options.D: whether they are men or women

questions.explanation: 作者一家三代都住在紐約，但祖父說 plimsolls、她說 sneakers、女兒說 kicks 或 vans，同一個地方、不同世代用詞不同，表示用詞也能看出「年紀」，選 A。C「在哪裡長大」是書中原本的論點，但空格前有 But…also，要填的是作者另外的新發現。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Look at the picture: a closed door with a sign that reads "Meeting Room" hanging on it. There is a potted plant on the left side of the door and an umbrella stand holding umbrellas on the right side. On the floor mat in front of the door, a rectangular piece of paper is sticking out from underneath the door. Look at the picture. There is ______ under the door.
questions.explanation: 看圖：門下方的地墊上露出一張長方形、像信封的紙，所以門下有的是 an envelope（信封）。盆栽 (plant) 在門的左邊、雨傘 (umbrella) 在右邊的傘架裡、牌子 (sign) 掛在門上，都不是在門下。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: My ______ hurts so much that I cannot even turn my head.
questions.explanation: 關鍵線索是「cannot even turn my head（連頭都轉不了）」，能讓人無法轉頭的是脖子 neck 在痛。arm（手臂）、knee（膝蓋）、stomach（胃）痛都不會直接影響轉頭。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Our school basketball team won the national game last night. We are so ______ them.
questions.explanation: 球隊贏得全國比賽，大家的心情應該是「以他們為榮」，be proud of 表示「為…感到驕傲」。popular with 是「受…歡迎」，sorry for 是「為…感到難過」，worried about 是「擔心」，都不符合贏球的語境。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Tomorrow is Sam's last day in the office. Nobody knows why he decided to ______ .
questions.explanation: 明天是 Sam 在辦公室的最後一天，表示他決定要離職，leave 在這裡是「離開（工作）」。hide（躲藏）、pack（打包）、walk（走路）都無法說明「最後一天上班」的原因。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: It's not a good idea to go mountain climbing in this bad ______ . We should wait until the typhoon goes away.
questions.explanation: 後句提到要等颱風 (typhoon) 離開，可知是天氣不好，bad weather 表示「惡劣天氣」。chance（機會）、dream（夢想）、habit（習慣）都和颱風無關。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Chris loves walking with Anna on snowy days, but Anna hates ______ very much.
questions.explanation: 空格指的是前面整件事「在下雪天散步 (walking on snowy days)」，代替一件事或一個動作要用單數代名詞 it。them 是複數，不能代替這件事；one 代替可數名詞；so 不能當 hate 的受詞。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Lora likes to eat bananas that are already a little brown on the outside, and so ______ I.
questions.explanation: 「so + 助動詞 + 主詞」表示「某人也一樣」，助動詞要配合前句的動詞。前句 likes 是一般動詞現在式，所以用 do：so do I（我也是）。如果前句是 be 動詞才用 am，完成式才用 have。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Your refrigerator shouldn't be making loud noises now, but if it ______ does, just give me a call and I'll come check it again.
questions.explanation: 前句說冰箱「現在應該不會再發出噪音了」，後句說「如果它仍然有噪音，就打電話給我」，still（仍然）表示狀況持續沒改善。already（已經）、finally（終於）不合語意；even（甚至）也無法表達「還是」的意思。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: After winning money in the card game, Jay decided to try again. He felt that he might also be ______ a second time.
questions.explanation: Jay 打牌贏了錢，決定再試一次，因為他覺得自己第二次也可能會「很幸運」，lucky 最符合。famous（有名的）、interested（有興趣的）、ready（準備好的）都和「贏錢、再試一次」的因果不搭。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: The knife doesn't cut very well. It's not as ______ as before.
questions.explanation: 刀子「切得不好」，表示它不像以前那麼鋒利，not as sharp as before。as + 原級形容詞 + as 是同等比較。bright（明亮的）、heavy（重的）、quick（快的）都不是形容刀子好不好切的字。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: John will stay with his sister until he ______ an apartment.
questions.explanation: until 引導的是表示時間的副詞子句，主要子句是未來式 (will stay) 時，時間子句要用現在式代替未來式，所以用 finds。常見錯誤是跟著寫 will find，但時間子句裡不能用 will。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Students ______ to go on the school trip should ask their parents first.
questions.explanation: 空格要修飾前面的 Students，說明是「想去校外教學的學生」，用關係代名詞 who 引導形容詞子句：Students who want to go...，後面的 should ask 才是主要動詞。B 少了關係代名詞，句子會有兩個動詞；C 多了 they，重複主詞；D 的 what 不能修飾人。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: The temple sits alone in the mountains at a height of 3,000m ______ sea level.
questions.explanation: 表示「海拔多少公尺」的固定說法是 above sea level（高於海平面）。寺廟在山上，高度 3,000 公尺當然是在海平面之上，below sea level 是「低於海平面」，at、in 都不能這樣搭配。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Patty spent several days planning to invite Charlie to dinner, ______ she couldn't say a word when they met.
questions.explanation: 前句說 Patty 花了好幾天計畫要邀請 Charlie 吃飯，後句卻說見面時一個字都說不出來，前後語意相反，要用 but（但是）。so 表結果、if 表條件、or 表選擇，都不能表達這種轉折。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: I can't tell you what I think of the movie because I ______ it. I'll probably watch it this Saturday.
questions.explanation: 說話者還沒看過電影（這週六可能才會去看），所以無法說出感想，要用現在完成式否定 haven't seen 表示「到目前為止還沒看過」。don't see 是現在簡單式，表習慣；won't see 表示將來不會看，和「週六可能會看」矛盾。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: The new guy at the help desk answers calls like a ______ . There are no ups and downs in his voice and you can't tell if he is happy or sad.
questions.explanation: 後句說他講話的聲音「沒有高低起伏、聽不出開心或難過」，這正是機器人說話的特點，所以說他接電話像個 robot（機器人）。father（父親）、foreigner（外國人）、radio（收音機）都沒有「毫無情緒起伏」的特徵。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Jasmine planned to spend her summer in the country, but right after she got there, she started to ______ the noise in the city.
questions.explanation: 句中用 but 轉折：Jasmine 原本計畫到鄉下過暑假，但一到那裡就開始「想念」城市的吵雜，miss 表示懷念、想念。enjoy（享受）、notice（注意到）不合理，因為她已經離開城市聽不到噪音；mind（介意）則和 but 的轉折方向不合。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: "Bad traffic" is perhaps the ______ excuse for being late when your boss knows it only takes you five minutes to walk to work.
questions.explanation: 老闆知道你走路上班只要五分鐘，這時用「塞車」當遲到理由根本說不過去，所以是「最糟糕的」藉口，選 worst。easiest（最簡單的）、oldest（最老的）、smartest（最聰明的）都無法表達這個藉口很爛的意思。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: The housework in Mr. and Mrs. Wang's family ______ between them and their kids. Everyone's got their own job to do.
questions.explanation: 家事是「被」大家分擔的，要用被動語態 be + p.p.；主詞 The housework 是不可數名詞，視為單數，所以用 is shared。B 的 are 不符合單數主詞；C、D 是主動語態，意思變成「家事去分擔」，不合理。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: I want to find another dentist because ______ pulled out a good tooth last time I went to him.
questions.explanation: 空格要當 because 子句的主詞，意思是「我的牙醫」拔了一顆好牙，所有格代名詞 mine 等於 my dentist，可避免重複 dentist。I 當主詞會變成「我自己拔了牙」，但句尾說是去看「他 (him)」時被拔的，不合理；me、myself 都不能當主詞。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text:
Mom: Linda, you've been playing computer games all evening! Have you finished your report?
Linda: Well, ______ most of it this afternoon, and I'll finish it by Friday.
questions.explanation: 時間副詞 this afternoon 指今天下午，媽媽說話時是晚上，所以下午做報告是已經發生的事，用過去簡單式 I did（我下午做完了大部分）。I'll do 是未來式，與「下午」已過去矛盾；I was doing 過去進行式強調某時點正在做，不適合說「完成大部分」。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text:
Passage: It was around eight o'clock on Saturday night. Philip was at home with his little brother, Jason. Jason was hungry and kept crying. But Philip couldn't cook and their father was not home yet because he was working late in the office. So Philip decided to take Jason out for some food.
Half an hour later, when they came back home, Philip was surprised to find that their father was talking to the police and a woman outside their house. He didn't know who the woman was. She looked scared and stood behind the police. Philip's father was very angry and kept shouting, "I didn't do anything wrong! I forgot my keys and was just trying to get into MY OWN HOUSE!" But the police didn't believe him until Philip ran to them and explained everything.
The police told Philip that the woman called 110 when she saw Philip's father trying to get into a house through a window. That was how it all happened.
Question: Why did Philip go out?

options.C: To ask the police for help.
options.D: To buy food for his brother.

questions.explanation: 文章第一段說弟弟 Jason 肚子餓一直哭，Philip 不會煮飯、爸爸又還沒回家，所以帶弟弟出去吃東西，答案是去幫弟弟買食物。他出門時根本不知道那個女人和警察的事，A、B、C 都是回家後才發生或與事實不符。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text:
Passage: It was around eight o'clock on Saturday night. Philip was at home with his little brother, Jason. Jason was hungry and kept crying. But Philip couldn't cook and their father was not home yet because he was working late in the office. So Philip decided to take Jason out for some food.
Half an hour later, when they came back home, Philip was surprised to find that their father was talking to the police and a woman outside their house. He didn't know who the woman was. She looked scared and stood behind the police. Philip's father was very angry and kept shouting, "I didn't do anything wrong! I forgot my keys and was just trying to get into MY OWN HOUSE!" But the police didn't believe him until Philip ran to them and explained everything.
The police told Philip that the woman called 110 when she saw Philip's father trying to get into a house through a window. That was how it all happened.
Question: Why was Philip's father angry?

options.B: The woman was hiding from him.
options.C: The police didn't believe what he said.
options.D: Philip and his brother went out at night.

questions.explanation: 爸爸一直大喊自己沒做錯事、只是忘了鑰匙想進自己家，但「警察不相信他」，直到 Philip 跑過去說明才解決，所以他生氣是因為警察不相信他的話。忘記鑰匙 (A) 是事情的起因，不是他生氣的對象；B、D 文中都沒有提到。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text:
Notice: BAKER'S KITCHEN, Since 1993. "We Give You the Taste of the Good Life." Want to be the first to bring our popular breads home? Here is when they come fresh out of the oven every day: French bread 7:30am; bread rolls 8:30am; croissants 9:30am (*Friday only); white bread 10:30am; bagels 11:30am; pretzels 2:30pm (*Friday only); challah 3:30pm; farm bread 4:30pm. All breads at half price after 8pm (after 7pm on Saturdays and Sundays). Become a Baker's Kitchen member for only $100 and you can save 10% on all your shopping at Baker's Kitchen. Business hours: Mon. to Fri., 7:30am to 9pm, Sat. & Sun., 7:30am to 8pm. (oven = 烤爐)
Question: Kevin is going to buy some fresh bread at Baker's Kitchen. He loves white bread, his mom likes farm bread, his father enjoys bagels, and his sister eats only challah. Which is the earliest possible time for him to get all these breads for his family?
questions.explanation: 查出爐時間：white bread 10:30am、bagels 11:30am、challah 3:30pm、farm bread 4:30pm。要一次買齊，至少要等到最晚出爐的 farm bread（4:30pm）之後，選項中最早可行的是 5:00pm。4:00pm 時 farm bread 還沒出爐；11:00am 時連 bagels 都還沒有。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text:
Notice: BAKER'S KITCHEN, Since 1993. "We Give You the Taste of the Good Life." Want to be the first to bring our popular breads home? Here is when they come fresh out of the oven every day: French bread 7:30am; bread rolls 8:30am; croissants 9:30am (*Friday only); white bread 10:30am; bagels 11:30am; pretzels 2:30pm (*Friday only); challah 3:30pm; farm bread 4:30pm. All breads at half price after 8pm (after 7pm on Saturdays and Sundays). Become a Baker's Kitchen member for only $100 and you can save 10% on all your shopping at Baker's Kitchen. Business hours: Mon. to Fri., 7:30am to 9pm, Sat. & Sun., 7:30am to 8pm. (oven = 烤爐)
Question: What do we know about Baker's Kitchen?

options.A: It is open five days a week.
options.B: Its breads are half price one hour before closing.
options.C: Its croissants and pretzels are sold on weekends.
options.D: Its members can save $100 when they shop on Fridays.

questions.explanation: 營業時間：平日 9pm 關門、半價從 8pm 開始；週末 8pm 關門、半價從 7pm 開始，兩者都是「關門前一小時」半價，所以選 B。它每天營業不是一週五天 (A)；可頌和蝴蝶餅只在週五有 (C)；會員費是 $100、享九折，不是省下 $100 (D)。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text:
Notice and map: INFORMATION ABOUT THE 2021 GREEN FESTIVAL. 1. The 2021 Green Festival will be held at Satyr's Park from April 1 to May 31. 2. You are welcome to take the Free Festival Bus at the Goat Street Station to the festival. 3. You can also go to the festival by metro (get off at the Koala Street Station or the Turtle Street Station) or by bus (take No. 28, 103, 125, 157, 259, 505, 908, or 1086). 4. During the festival, Fox Street is closed; no cars can enter the street. 5. Garden Square won't be open for car parking; there will be a farmers' market at the square during the festival. 6. During the festival, Faun's Weekend Flower Market will be open every day from 8am to 2pm. Map layout (from north to south: Cow Road, Bear Road, Lion Road, Hippo Road; from west to east: Goat Street, Duck Street, Koala Street, Hen Street, Fox Street, Puppy Street, Turtle Street): Block between Cow Road/Bear Road, Duck St/Hen St area has the Free Festival Bus stop and a Metro station (west side); the block on the far east between Cow Road/Bear Road (near Turtle Street) has a Metro station and bus stops for No. 28, 103, 125, 259. Block between Bear Road/Lion Road: west block (Goat St/Koala St) has bus stops for No. 28, 157, 259; middle block has Faun's Weekend Flower Market; Fox Street (closed to cars) runs between Faun's Weekend Flower Market and Satyr's Park (site of the Green Festival), both in the middle of this row. Block between Lion Road/Hippo Road: middle block (Koala St/Puppy St) has Garden Square (Farmers' Market) with a Metro station and bus stops for No. 125, 157, 908, 1086; the east block (Puppy St/Turtle St) has bus stops for No. 28, 125, 505. (recommend = 推薦)
Question: What is recommended to people who want to visit the festival?

options.A: Using the free festival bus service.
options.B: Visiting the festival on the weekend.
options.C: Entering Satyr's Park from Fox Street.
options.D: Parking in Garden Square and walking to the festival.

questions.explanation: 公告第 2 點 You are welcome to take the Free Festival Bus... 就是在推薦大家搭免費接駁車。花市每天都開，沒有推薦週末去 (B)；Fox Street 活動期間封閉 (C)；Garden Square 不開放停車，改成農夫市集 (D)。

Question: What can we learn about the farmers' market from the map?

options.A: The farmers' market is next to the flower market.
options.B: The farmers' market and the festival are on the same block.
options.C: You can go to the farmers' market by taking Bus No. 157 to Puppy Street.
options.D: The nearest metro station to the farmers' market is the Koala Street Station.

questions.explanation: 地圖上農夫市集在 Garden Square，同一街區靠 Koala Street 那側就有捷運站，所以最近的捷運站是 Koala Street Station。農夫市集和花市、Satyr's Park 之間隔著 Lion Road，不相鄰也不同街區 (A、B)；Puppy Street 旁的公車站只有 28、125、505，沒有 157 (C)。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text:
Story 1: Yan lived a good life in a big house. One day he invited a friend to dinner at his house. However, on the dinner table there was only one small dish of one small fish. The friend looked quietly at the fish. It was no bigger than a finger. Then he asked Yan if he could borrow a lamp. "What for?" Yan asked. "Well, it's so dark in here," the friend said with a dry smile, "I can't see the other delicious dishes you've prepared for me."
Story 2: Chang kept a lot of ducks and chickens on his farm. One day, his best friend came to visit him. At noon, Chang told his friend that he couldn't let him stay for lunch because there wasn't much food to eat. The friend looked out at Chang's farm animals for a moment. Then he asked Chang if he had a big knife. "Yes, but what for?" Chang asked. "I'm thinking about killing the horse I rode here so we'll have something for lunch," the friend said. "But how are you going to go home without it?" "Well, you wouldn't mind lending me one of your many ducks or chickens so I can ride it home, would you?" (likely = 可能)
Question: What kind of people do Yan's and Chang's friends most likely think Yan and Chang are?
questions.explanation: 兩個故事裡的朋友都在「話中有話」地諷刺主人：Yan 請客只端出一條手指大的小魚，朋友假裝太暗要借燈找「其他菜」；Chang 養了很多雞鴨卻說沒東西吃，朋友說要殺自己的馬當午餐。可見朋友都覺得 Yan 和 Chang 很小氣、不願意分享 (don't like to share)。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text:
Passage (TAINAN CORNERS): Usually, people visit bookstores to buy books. But those who walk into Cotoha come to see its owner, Chen Bing-Hong. They bring him books with different problems. Some have lost their covers, some are missing a few pages, and some have pages that are falling out. Chen can always fix the books and make them whole again.
Chen sees himself as a doctor. He says that books, like people, get sick and need help. In Taiwan, there are not many "doctors" like him, and most of them work for big libraries and museums. If big libraries and museums are hospitals, Chen's bookstore is a health center. Big libraries and museums fix important old books with serious problems, and Chen helps people with books that have smaller problems. However, the smaller size of the problems doesn't mean Chen's job is less important.
Chen gave an example of a science book he once worked on. It was very old and half of its cover was lost. Its owner still wanted to keep it because it was a gift from a teacher who helped him follow his dream of studying science. When he got his book back, he was very surprised at the new-old book. He felt he was brought back to the days with his teacher. Seeing the owner's smile made Chen happy, because smiles like that are what his magic is for.
Question: Why does the writer talk about doctors and a health center in the reading?

options.B: To talk about Chen's future plans.
options.C: To explain Chen's love for books.
options.D: To show why bookstores are important.

questions.explanation: 作者把陳炳宏比喻成「書的醫生」，把大型圖書館和博物館比作醫院、他的書店比作健康中心：大館修嚴重的古書，他幫一般人處理小毛病的書。這個比喻是為了說明他提供的服務是什麼，選 A。文中沒提到他的未來計畫 (B)，也不是在說書店為何重要 (D)。

questions.question_text:
Web article "A Delicious Surprise and Welcome Change" by Karl Falk, June 1, 2016 (habibi hawara, https://www.refugeefriendly.org/habibi-hawara/), with a map showing Austria and Syria: In Austria, there are not many restaurants like Habibi & Hawara. Here you can enjoy Austrian and Syrian food together. Two Austrians, Martin Rohla and David Kreytenberg, started this yummy plan from their experience of working with refugees.
Every year, thousands of people have to leave their homes and families because of war in their countries. So many of them go to Austria that some people in the country think they have become a problem. They are afraid refugees may take away their jobs and they don't feel safe around them, either. But Rohla and Kreytenberg would beg to differ: The refugees don't have to be a problem. They want to help them start a new life. They invited refugees to meetings and found that some of them were cooks back in Syria. So the idea of Habibi & Hawara was born—a restaurant that brings together Austrian and Syrian food. "The two worlds far away from each other meet together," Kreytenberg said.
But Rohla and Kreytenberg want to do more than just give the refugees work. They want their best workers to buy the restaurant in the end. They hope that Habibi & Hawara is not just a one-time plan and that other Austrians will join them and help more refugees. (refugee = 難民, war = 戰爭)
Question: According to the reading, why did Rohla and Kreytenberg open Habibi & Hawara?

options.A: To help refugees live better in Austria.
options.B: To collect money to help Syria fight the war.
options.C: To help Austrians learn about the war in Syria.
options.D: To help refugees go back to their home countries.

questions.explanation: 文中說兩人想幫助難民「開始新生活」，發現有些難民在敘利亞曾是廚師，才開了這家餐廳，後來還希望有更多奧地利人一起幫助難民，所以目的是幫難民在奧地利過得更好 (A)。文中沒有提到募款支持戰爭、讓奧地利人了解戰爭或送難民回國。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text:
Article "VOICES OF PEOPLE" by Ellen Zimmer: If you want to learn about bringing back extinct animals, reading John Smith's Back from the Dead is a good start. But I have to say I can't agree with everything he says.
From his book, I can see Smith is an advocate of bringing extinct animals back. He says we have lost many animals because we made their living spaces too dirty. He also thinks we must do everything we can to bring them back. However, I don't know how much time and money we would need to make the world a better place for them, and honestly no one knows if they could actually come back.
Smith also says that bringing back extinct animals may be good for us. He talks about an extinct frog that grew tadpoles in its stomach. Some women's babies die before they are born, and Smith believes bringing back the frog may be an answer to the problem. According to him, by studying how the tadpoles grow inside the frog's stomach, we might be able to find new ways to help these women successfully keep their babies. But I don't think things are as easy as Smith thinks. We have spent ten years and millions of dollars on this kind of frog, but all we have got are only a few dead frog eggs. If we can't see a real frog, how can we be sure women will get the help they need?
Dr. Solomon Wang from the Animal Saving Office says the study of bringing back extinct animals is "throwing good money after bad." And he's right. A lot of hard work has been put into this expensive dream, but we haven't seen anything come out of it. So should we still keep going down this road? (extinct = 絕種的, tadpole = 蝌蚪)
Question: What does it mean when someone is an advocate of something?

options.A: They talk a lot but do little about it.
options.B: They believe it is good and should be done.
options.C: They have had some bad experiences with it.
options.D: They are one of the first people who have done it.

questions.concept_tag: 上下文詞義與指代推測
questions.explanation: advocate 後面接著說明 Smith 認為我們「必須盡一切努力讓絕種動物回來」，可見他是支持、提倡這件事的人，所以 advocate 是「認為某事是好的、應該去做」的人 (B)。文中沒有說他光說不做 (A)，也沒說他是第一個做的人 (D)。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text:
Article "A HISTORY LESSON ON THE PANDEMIC" (2020.10.29): Since the Covid-19 pandemic started, people have begun "social distancing"—keeping a safe space between you and anyone you don't live with. Though it has been a very popular topic this year, social distancing __40__ . In fact, it was widely used in the U.S. in the flu pandemic in 1918. But how well did it work? The Americans' experience can tell us whether it really saved lives.
Chart data ("Each week's numbers of deaths per 100,000 people from September 11, 1918 through February 19, 1919," 24 weeks, grey bands = social distancing time): Portland — total deaths per 100,000 after 24 weeks: 506; two grey (social distancing) bands, roughly weeks 6-11 and weeks 14-19; the death curve has a first peak (~62) around week 9, dips to about 20 around week 12-13, rises to a second peak (~47) around week 19, then falls to near 0 by week 24. New York — total: 453; one grey band roughly weeks 2-9; curve has one sharp peak (~88) around week 7, then drops quickly to near 0 by week 12, with a small bump (~15) around week 20. Denver — total: 631; two grey bands roughly weeks 5-9 and weeks 11-15; curve has a first peak (~55) around week 7, dips to about 33 around week 10, rises to a second peak (~70) around week 13, then declines to near 0 by weeks 20-24. Pittsburgh — total: 807; one grey band roughly weeks 4-11; curve rises steeply to a single peak (~120) around week 9, then declines gradually, with a small bump (~18) around week 21. (pandemic = (疾病的)大流行, per = 每(一))
From the picture, we can see that __41__ started social distancing earlier than the other three cities. This helped the city keep the number of deaths down. Besides taking early action, keeping the action long enough was also important in fighting the pandemic. The picture shows that Portland and Denver did well in the first few weeks. However, both cities __42__ , and the numbers of deaths climbed again.
But there was one thing Portland did right. The city used several ways of social distancing at the same time to deal with the pandemic. __43__ , sick people were kept away from healthy ones; schools were closed; public activities were not allowed. All these were useful in keeping people safe.
The lessons of the 1918 pandemic bring us hope. While we are still learning to fight Covid-19, social distancing may be the best way to get us through the dark days, at least for now.
Question 40: choose the best word(s) for blank 40.
questions.explanation: 空格後緊接 In fact, it was widely used in the U.S. in the flu pandemic in 1918（事實上它早在 1918 年流感大流行時就被廣泛使用），說明社交距離「並不是新的概念」，選 A。Though 引導的前半句說今年很熱門，後半句用「不是新點子」形成對比；B、C、D 都和後面「1918 年就用過」的說明接不起來。

New York — total: 453; one grey band roughly weeks 2-9 (the earliest-starting social distancing band among all four cities); curve has one sharp peak (~88) around week 7, then drops quickly to near 0 by week 12, with a small bump (~15) around week 20. Denver — total: 631; two grey bands roughly weeks 5-9 and weeks 11-15; curve has a first peak (~55) around week 7, dips to about 33 around week 10, rises to a second peak (~70) around week 13, then declines to near 0 by weeks 20-24. Pittsburgh — total: 807; one grey band roughly weeks 4-11; curve rises steeply to a single peak (~120) around week 9, then declines gradually, with a small bump (~18) around week 21. (pandemic = (疾病的)大流行, per = 每(一))
From the picture, we can see that __41__ started social distancing earlier than the other three cities. This helped the city keep the number of deaths down. Besides taking early action, keeping the action long enough was also important in fighting the pandemic. The picture shows that Portland and Denver did well in the first few weeks. However, both cities __42__ , and the numbers of deaths climbed again.
But there was one thing Portland did right. The city used several ways of social distancing at the same time to deal with the pandemic. __43__ , sick people were kept away from healthy ones; schools were closed; public activities were not allowed. All these were useful in keeping people safe.
The lessons of the 1918 pandemic bring us hope. While we are still learning to fight Covid-19, social distancing may be the best way to get us through the dark days, at least for now.
Question 41: choose the best word(s) for blank 41.
questions.explanation: 看四張圖的灰色區塊（社交距離期間）：New York 的灰色區塊大約從第 2 週就開始，比其他三個城市都早，而且它 24 週的總死亡數 453 是四城中最低，正好符合下一句「這幫助該城市壓低死亡數」。

questions.subject: english_read

The lessons of the 1918 pandemic bring us hope. While we are still learning to fight Covid-19, social distancing may be the best way to get us through the dark days, at least for now.
Question 42: choose the best word(s) for blank 42.

options.C: began social distancing a second time
options.D: had the most days of social distancing

questions.explanation: 前一句強調「措施要維持夠久」也很重要；圖中 Portland 和 Denver 的第一段灰色區塊結束後，死亡曲線又往上升，所以是它們太早停止社交距離 (stopped social distancing too soon)，死亡數才又攀升。C 雖然圖上看得到第二段灰色區塊，但「又開始實施」不會是死亡數上升的原因，也接不上 However 的轉折。

Question 43: choose the best word(s) for blank 43.
questions.explanation: 前一句說 Portland 同時使用了好幾種社交距離的方法，空格後列出隔離病人、關閉學校、禁止公共活動等具體做法，這是在舉例，所以用 For example。Also 是補充、However 是轉折、At first 是時間順序，都不符合「前面概括、後面舉例」的關係。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Look at the picture. A ______ is flying over the houses. (The picture shows a street scene with houses/shops, a bird perched on a rooftop, a plane flying in the sky above the houses, a boy flying a kite near the ground, and a butterfly near flowers.)
questions.explanation: 題目問「飛在房子上方」的東西。圖中飛機在屋頂上方的天空飛，所以選 plane。鳥是停在屋頂上，並沒有在飛；風箏和蝴蝶都在低處的路邊與花叢旁，不在房子上方。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: When I was a teenager, I was very ______ . But now, it's easier for me to talk to people.
questions.explanation: 關鍵在 But now, it's easier for me to talk to people（但現在我比較容易跟人說話了），用 But 表示和以前相反，可推知以前「不太敢跟人說話」，也就是 shy（害羞的）。happy、lazy、popular 都和「不敢跟人說話」對不起來。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Lena doesn't want to go ______ with John because she is afraid of water.
questions.explanation: Lena 不想去是因為 she is afraid of water（她怕水），所以空格應是和水有關的活動 sailing（駕帆船、航行）。go + V-ing 表示去從事某活動；跳舞、健行、購物都和水無關。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Cindy enjoys ______ her dad read stories to her before bed.
questions.explanation: enjoy 後面要接動名詞（enjoy + V-ing），所以選 listening to。「listen to + 人 + 原形動詞」表示聽某人做某事，所以後面是 her dad read stories。to listen to、listen to、listens to 都不能直接放在 enjoy 後面。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Dad is busy cooking in the kitchen. Dinner will be ______ in ten minutes.
questions.explanation: 爸爸正在廚房忙著煮飯，所以晚餐「再十分鐘就好了」，be ready 表示準備好。free（免費的／有空的）、full（飽的；滿的）、medium（中等的）放進句子都不合語意。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: There are so many new ______ in the office. It'll take me some time to remember who is who.
questions.explanation: 後句說「我要花一些時間才能記得誰是誰」，表示辦公室裡有很多新的人。new faces 是「新面孔」的意思，指新來的人，所以選 faces。ideas、rules、tools 都不會讓人需要記「誰是誰」。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: I feel like a ______ . I was looking for my keys for hours but they have been in my pocket the whole time.
questions.explanation: 我找鑰匙找了好幾個小時，結果鑰匙一直都在自己口袋裡，這種情況會覺得自己像個「傻瓜」，feel like a fool 就是覺得自己很蠢。ghost（鬼）、king（國王）、stranger（陌生人）都和這個情境不符。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Mr. and Mrs. Wu have three daughters. Two are in high school, and ______ is in elementary school.
questions.explanation: 三個女兒中兩個唸高中，剩下的「最後那一個」唸小學。在限定範圍內說完一部分後，指剩下的最後一個要用 the other。each 表示「每一個」、the one 和 the next 都不能表示「剩下的那個」。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: It is hard for trees to ______ along this beach because of the strong winds from the sea.
questions.explanation: 因為海邊的強風，樹木很難在這片海灘「生長」，所以選 grow。最容易誤選 blow（吹），但吹的是風，不是樹；build（建造）、follow（跟隨）語意也不通。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Christmas ______ and I want to visit my aunt abroad. Do you have any plans yet?
questions.explanation: 後面問「你有任何計畫了嗎？」，可知聖誕節是「即將到來」的事，用現在進行式 is coming 表示即將發生的事。came 和 was coming 是過去式，與後面的 want、Do you have 時態不合；comes 單純陳述事實，不如 is coming 能表達「快到了」的語感。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Jo won't be happy if you're late for his party tonight, so ______ sure that you arrive on time.
questions.explanation: so 後面是一個對聽者下指令的祈使句，祈使句用原形動詞開頭，所以選 make（make sure 確定、務必）。makes、to make、is making 都不能當祈使句的開頭，而且空格前面沒有主詞。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: You may have a long drive because of the terrible ______ . There are usually a lot of cars and buses during this time.
questions.explanation: 後句說這段時間通常有很多汽車和公車，可知路上會塞車，terrible traffic 指「糟糕的交通狀況」，所以會開很久。experience（經驗）、machine（機器）、service（服務）都無法和「車很多」的線索連結。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: In the future, there will ______ be greater basketball players than Stephen Curry, but now we believe he is the best!
questions.explanation: 後面用 but now we believe he is the best（但現在我們相信他是最好的），前半句是對未來不確定的推測：將來「或許」會有更偉大的球員，所以選 perhaps。never 會變成「將來絕不會有」，和 but 的轉折語氣矛盾；again、already 語意不通。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: I guess the rainwater has come in from the kitchen. See? ______ of the windows are closed except the one in the kitchen.
questions.concept_tag: 數量詞與主詞動詞一致
questions.explanation: 說話者推測雨水是從廚房進來的，證據是「除了廚房那扇以外，所有的窗戶都關著」，所以選 All。except 常和 all、every 搭配表示「除了…之外全部」。Both 只能指兩個；Most、Some 則不能證明只有廚房那扇開著。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: ______ machines have been used to pick fruits for a long time, they were not used on strawberry farms until several years ago.
questions.explanation: 前半句說機器用來採水果已經很久了，後半句說直到幾年前才用在草莓園，兩句語意相反，要用表示讓步的 Although（雖然）。注意英文用了 although 就不能再加 but。Because、Before、If 都無法表達這種轉折。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: There are online videos that teach you exercises you can do at home. They'll ______ you a trip to the gym, and some money too.
questions.explanation: 在家看線上影片運動，就不用跑一趟健身房，也能省錢。save + 人 + 事物 表示「替某人省下…」，所以選 save。最容易誤選 cost（花費），但 cost 表示要付出代價，意思正好相反；give、keep 語意不通。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Jane's parents are always happy to see their grandchildren, but mine ______ less so when I visit them with my kids.
questions.concept_tag: 數量詞與主詞動詞一致
questions.explanation: mine 在這裡指 my parents（我的父母），是複數，所以 be 動詞用 are。less so 是代替前面的 happy，意思是「我的父母就沒那麼開心」，前面對應的是 be 動詞（are happy），所以不用助動詞 do／does。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: Before she ______ about it, you should tell Daphne you broke her favorite cup.
questions.explanation: Before 引導的是時間副詞子句，主要子句是未來的建議（you should tell…），時間子句要用現在式代替未來式，所以用 asks。will ask 是常見陷阱，時間子句中不能用 will；asked、was asking 是過去時態，不合語意。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text: It was very windy this morning. Some of the shirts on the balcony were blown away ______ in the pond.
questions.concept_tag: 分詞構句與感官使役動詞
questions.explanation: 襯衫「被吹走，然後掉進池塘」，兩個動作都是過去發生的，用 and 連接兩個對等的過去式動詞 were blown away and fell。fall 的過去式是 fell，fallen 是過去分詞；沒有 and 的 fell 會讓一句出現兩個動詞而不通。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text:
Passage: Rex is a dog that lives at the bakery next to our school. He is cute and friendly. Every morning, he stands in front of the school to welcome everybody. We all see Rex as one of us. But one Monday morning, I was surprised that Rex was not there to say hello to us. "Rex is in the hospital. He was hit by a car last night," my classmate told me. We went to see Rex in the hospital that day after school. Two weeks later, Rex was much better, and we decided to take him for a walk every evening. Because of the exercise, Rex became healthier and stronger. Soon he could happily run and jump again. He is now as handsome and strong as before!

Question: What happened to Rex?
questions.explanation: 同學說 Rex 住院了，因為 He was hit by a car last night（昨晚被車撞），可知 Rex 受傷了，got hurt 就是「受傷」。文中沒有提到走失、咬人或吃太多。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text:
Passage: Rex is a dog that lives at the bakery next to our school. He is cute and friendly. Every morning, he stands in front of the school to welcome everybody. We all see Rex as one of us. But one Monday morning, I was surprised that Rex was not there to say hello to us. "Rex is in the hospital. He was hit by a car last night," my classmate told me. We went to see Rex in the hospital that day after school. Two weeks later, Rex was much better, and we decided to take him for a walk every evening. Because of the exercise, Rex became healthier and stronger. Soon he could happily run and jump again. He is now as handsome and strong as before!

Question: How did the writer help Rex?

options.C: By taking him to see a doctor.
options.D: By looking for a new home for him.

questions.explanation: 文中說兩週後 Rex 好多了，作者和同學決定每天傍晚帶牠去散步，Because of the exercise（因為運動）Rex 變得更健康強壯，所以作者是靠「讓牠運動」幫助牠。最容易誤選 C：作者只是放學後去醫院「探望」Rex，並不是帶牠去看醫生；報警、幫牠找新家文中都沒提。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text:
Chat (Friends Forever Group (3): Jenny, Linda, Mark):
Jenny: Hey guys, guess what? I'm getting married next year!
Linda: Wow, I'm so happy for you. (laughing emoji)
Mark: I have good news too! I just got the job I've wanted so much.
Linda: Come on, Mark. Don't start again.
Mark: (confused emoji, question marks)
Linda: You're stealing Jenny's thunder. Jenny was telling us about her big news. It's very important to her. And you want us to hear about your new job now?
Mark: I didn't mean that. I just...
Jenny: I agree. Last time when we were talking about how delicious Linda's cake was, you started telling us about the chocolate cake you made at home.
Mark: All right, all right, my problem. Sorry, Jenny. I'll never do that again. So do you want to know what job I got?
Linda: MARK!!

Question: What do we know about Mark from the dialogue?

options.B: He is looking for a new job.
options.C: He did not like Linda's cake.
options.D: He is getting married to Jenny.

questions.explanation: Jenny 正在宣布婚訊時，Mark 插話講自己找到新工作，Linda 立刻說 Come on, Mark. Don't start again. 並責怪他，最後還大喊 MARK!!，可見 Mark 讓 Linda 不高興。B 錯在 Mark 已經找到工作；C 錯在 Mark 是講自己做的蛋糕，沒說不喜歡 Linda 的蛋糕；D 要結婚的是 Jenny，文中沒說對象是 Mark。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text:
Chat (Friends Forever Group (3): Jenny, Linda, Mark):
Jenny: Hey guys, guess what? I'm getting married next year!
Linda: Wow, I'm so happy for you. (laughing emoji)
Mark: I have good news too! I just got the job I've wanted so much.
Linda: Come on, Mark. Don't start again.
Mark: (confused emoji, question marks)
Linda: You're stealing Jenny's thunder. Jenny was telling us about her big news. It's very important to her. And you want us to hear about your new job now?
Mark: I didn't mean that. I just...
Jenny: I agree. Last time when we were talking about how delicious Linda's cake was, you started telling us about the chocolate cake you made at home.
Mark: All right, all right, my problem. Sorry, Jenny. I'll never do that again. So do you want to know what job I got?
Linda: MARK!!

(Vocabulary note: likely 可能)
Question: Which is most likely an example of stealing someone's thunder?

options.A: Dennis never changes his mind except when his wife tells him to.
options.B: Melisa tells Tom she'll go to the party but tells her mom she'll stay home.
options.C: Jeff tells everyone he'll move abroad when Ivy is still telling them about her baby.
options.D: Alisa says she doesn't care what we have for lunch but also doesn't like the restaurant we chose.

questions.explanation: 從 Linda 的解釋可知，stealing someone's thunder 是指「別人正在分享自己的重要消息時，你搶著講自己的事，把大家的注意力搶走」，也就是搶了別人的風頭。C 選項中 Ivy 還在說她寶寶的事，Jeff 就宣布自己要出國，正是這種情形。A、B、D 分別在說聽老婆的話、說話前後不一、嘴上說不在意卻又挑剔，都不是搶風頭。

questions.subject: english_read
questions.question_text:
Notice: Buy a White Lake City Card When You're in the City
① With any of the Cards, you can:
- visit the city by metro, bus, or train as many times as you want.*
- take one child under 12 with you for free.
- save 20% on tickets to public museums.
② The 1-day, 3-day, and 5-day Cards are for trips from Monday to Friday, and the Weekend Card is for trips on weekends and holidays.
③ Check the map and buy the right Card for the zones you'll be entering.
Card prices: 1-day: Zone1 $20, Zones1-2 $40, Zones1-3 $60. 3-day: Zone1 $40, Zones1-2 $60, Zones1-3 $80. 5-day: Zone1 $50, Zones1-2 $80, Zones1-3 $110. Weekend: Zone1 $30, Zones1-2 $50, Zones1-3 $80.
* The Cards are only for trips inside the three zones.
Locations: (a) White Lake Main Station, (b) Museum of White Lake City History, (c) Museum of Modern Art, (d) White Lake, (e) White Lake Castle, (f) White Lake Airport.

Question: What can you do with a White Lake City Card?

options.B: Visit any public museum in the city for free.
options.C: Take a train to places out of the three zones.
options.D: Move around the city by metro as much as you want.

questions.explanation: 告示第①點寫著，持卡可以 visit the city by metro, bus, or train as many times as you want，也就是可以無限次搭乘地鐵在城裡移動，所以選 D。A 錯：是可免費帶一名 12 歲以下兒童，打八折的是公立博物館門票；B 錯：博物館是打八折不是免費；C 錯：星號註明卡片只能用於三個區域內。

questions.question_text:
